For information relating to evidence requirements for conflicting trade marks, refer to Part 28 of this Manual."},{"ref":"TMA1995/s41","quote":"(1) An application for the registration of a trade mark must be rejected if the trade mark is not capable of distinguishing the applicant’s goods or services in respect of which the trade mark is sought to be registered (the designated goods or services) from the goods or services of other persons."},{"ref":"TMA1995/s41","quote":"(3) This subsection applies to a trade mark if: (a) the trade mark is not to any extent inherently adapted to distinguish the designated goods or services from the goods or services of other persons; and (b) the applicant has not used the trade mark before the filing date in respect of the application to such an extent that the trade mark does in fact distinguish the designated goods or services as being those of the applicant."},{"ref":"TMM/Part32A/x-annex-6---how-to-supply-evidence-of-use-of-a-trade-mark-for-plants-and-or-plant-material#1~1","quote":"“Evidence of use” is usually information about: Use already being made of your trade mark in Australia or overseas: The information must show that your trade mark has become, or is likely to become, identified as a trade source for your goods and not simply an alternate name for the goods themselves. PLEASE NOTE: In connection with plant material, “trade name” is not synonymous with “trade mark”. While it is unlikely that evidence could overcome the problem in the conventional sense of examination, particularly in relation to s41(3), it may be possible to accept the trade mark with a condition of registration if the evidence demonstrates use of a trade mark in conjunction with genus, species and variety name information."},{"ref":"TMA1995/s41","quote":"(4) This subsection applies to a trade mark if: (a) the trade mark is, to some extent, but not sufficiently, inherently adapted to distinguish the designated goods or services from the goods or services of other persons; and (b) the trade mark does not and will not distinguish the designated goods or services as being those of the applicant having regard to the combined effect of the following: (i) the extent to which the trade mark is inherently adapted to distinguish the goods or services from the goods or services of other persons; (ii) the use, or intended use, of the trade mark by the …"}],"answer":"## Scope and legal requirement
These evidence guidelines are **Manual practice for section 41**, not legislation. They do not cover evidence for conflicting trade marks; the Manual directs readers to Part 28 for that. [1]

**The Act:** section 41 requires rejection if the mark is not capable of distinguishing the applicant’s designated goods or services from those of others. For a mark with no inherent adaptation to distinguish, section 41(3) requires use **before the filing date** to such an extent that the mark actually distinguishes the applicant’s goods or services. Planned use alone does not satisfy that particular requirement. [2–3]

## What your evidence needs to show — Manual practice
The central point is **trade source, not merely a plant name**. Evidence of existing use in Australia or overseas must show that the mark has become, or is likely to become, identified as a trade source rather than simply an alternative name for the goods. In some cases, specific, documented preparations for Australian use may demonstrate its potential to identify trade source. [4]

Show how the mark appears alongside the relevant **genus, species and variety names**. A plant “trade name” is not necessarily a trade mark: it may merely describe a single variety. The Manual says the mark should be applied to several different plants or, if used for a single plant, always alongside that plant’s accepted scientific and variety names. [4–5]

## How to provide it — Manual practice
Supply a **declaration**, preferably electronically through online services, observing the file-type and size guidelines. It must be made by you as applicant, an appropriate company officer or authorised employee, or someone authorised to declare on your behalf, such as a lawyer or trade mark attorney. [6–7]

The declaration must have the matter’s title, use the first person, identify the declarant and their address, and—where applicable—the company, its address and the declarant’s position. It must state the date and place, use consecutively numbered paragraphs confined to one subject where practicable, state the declarant’s belief that it is true and correct, and be signed. The online declaration form incorporates these requirements. [7]

## What to include — Manual practice
Identify who uses or intends to use the mark: you or your company, an authorised user, or a predecessor in title. For **actual use**, include: [8]
- First use to sell goods: year and, if possible, month.
- Where it has been used: Australian States or regions and/or overseas countries.
- The goods sold under it.
- Examples of use, attaching digital images of packaging, advertising or promotional material.
- Annual advertising and promotional expenditure in Australian dollars.
- Annual turnover in Australian dollars for goods sold under the mark; the figures must cover only goods in the application.
- Other supporting information and digital images showing how it has been used. [8]

For **intended use**, provide comprehensive business plans or other documents demonstrating a definite intention to use the mark, with copies attached. The supplied intended-use checklist cuts off, so I cannot give its complete contents. [9]

## Qualification
The Manual cautions that evidence is unlikely to overcome a plant-name objection in conventional examination, particularly under section 41(3). It describes possible acceptance with a condition of registration where evidence demonstrates use alongside genus, species and variety information; this is practice guidance, not a prediction about your application. [10]

The supplied section 41(4) text expressly refers to use or intended use but is also truncated, so it does not provide the complete statutory test. [11]"}
